_why: Sites where a performance budget is deliberately measured by a SINGLE clock delta instead of min-of-K. An entry is a decision, not a proof: each one has to say which kind it is and, in its own `note`, why this site is different from the other 22 (see REQ-A850 / F-DEV-106). The list is empty on purpose — every budget assertion in the tree is bound through fastest()/fastestAsync() (`src/__tests__/perfBudget.ts`), and a site may only be added here with an argument that survives being read out loud.

measures-machine-not-code.reason: The assertion's verdict is about how loaded the machine was, not about the code. Nothing in this repo has a legitimate use for that.
measures-machine-not-code.note: Kept as a defined kind with no members so that adding the first member is an explicit, reviewable act rather than a new category.

semantics-not-performance.reason: The measurement is a claim about TIME ITSELF (a timeout, a debounce, a dwell), not about the code's cost — so it must be single-shot, and the budget is a semantic constant rather than a performance envelope.
semantics-not-performance.note: Correct member shape: file::ident, kind semantics-not-performance, plus a note naming the semantic constant (e.g. 'the 300ms debounce from lib/debounce.ts') and the test that would fail if the constant were wrong.
